data_quality_notes: ML_ALLpyq_1.md contains 6 distinct examination papers plus a third-party solved study guide ('Created by @prantehare') that reproduces the Supplementary Winter 2025 paper with answers. The guide was counted once as the paper itself and was not treated as an official answer key.

All objective answers are ai_solved. For Supplementary Winter 2025 they agree with the third-party guide. P3 Q1 (house-price problem) has two defensible options (Regression, Supervised Learning); option c follows the guide and confidence is medium.

Subject codes differ: BTAIC502 (Semester V, AI&DS and allied) appears in 2 papers; BTCOC603 / BTCOC603_Y23 (Semester VI, CSE/Computer Engineering) in 4 papers. All were analysed together because the subject is Machine Learning; confirm this suits your Semester 5 branch.
Supplementary Winter 2025 was held on 16/01/2026; exam_year is recorded as 2025 as printed on the paper. Winter 2023 is headed 'Regular & Supplementary', so exam_type is 'unknown'.
Marks for Summer 2025 MCQs are null because the paper does not print per-question marks; the other papers print 1 mark per MCQ.

Data missing from the source text (tables not captured): Winter 2023 Q2(c) price table, Q4(a) buyer dataset and Q5(a) Naive Bayes dataset; Supplementary Winter 2024 Q5(a) Find-S dataset. Summer 2025 Q6(c) wording appears garbled ('differ from regular hierarchical clustering'). Supplementary Summer 2024 Q2(b) table labels are inconsistent in the source; values were copied as printed.
page_number is null throughout because pages are not reliably identifiable in the merged file.

Mapping judgement calls (strict five-unit syllabus): activation-function MCQs -> Introduction to Deep Neural Networks; Find-S -> Hypothesis space and inductive bias; train/validation/test and validation-set items -> Cross-validation; dendrogram, agglomerative/divisive and hierarchical clustering -> Adaptive hierarchical clustering; kernel trick in SVM -> Kernel SVM. Review these if the official detailed syllabus says otherwise.

Gradient descent (4 appearances), bias-variance (2), regularisation (2), CNN, SVR and BNN/feedback-network questions are not named in the strict syllabus and are kept in partially_aligned_questions, not the main bank. Gradient descent is asked often, so consider revising it with Linear regression and Backpropagation.
